title: There's No Lead in Your Pencil
text:
Pencil 'lead' is graphite mixed with clay, pressed into rods and fired in a kiln, then glued between grooved cedar slats and sliced into pencils. A big graphite find in 1500s England was mistaken for lead, and the name stuck. More clay makes a harder, lighter line; more graphite a softer, darker one.
